docs.title: Evaluation datasets
docs.text:
The repository has two related dataset interfaces:

  • agentic_v2_eval.datasets loads benchmark tasks for Python evaluation code.
  • The runtime server lists and pages through repository and local datasets for the dashboard.

Neither interface executes a workflow or scores a result by itself.

docs.title: Benchmark API
docs.text:
The evaluation package exposes these benchmark identifiers:

ID Source type Main use swe-bench Hugging Face Repository issue resolution swe-bench-verified Hugging Face Human-validated SWE-bench subset swe-bench-lite Hugging Face Smaller SWE-bench subset humaneval Hugging Face Python function generation humaneval-plus Hugging Face HumanEval with additional tests mbpp Hugging Face Basic Python problems mbpp-sanitized Hugging Face Cleaned MBPP subset codeclash GitHub Multi-file development tasks custom-local Local files Repository-defined tasks

The registry is defined in tools/agents/benchmarks/datasets.py. Query it at runtime instead of copying dataset sizes or URLs into application code:

from agentic_v2_eval.datasets import (
    get_benchmark_definition,
    list_benchmarks,
    load_benchmark,
)

print(list_benchmarks())
definition = get_benchmark_definition("humaneval")
print(definition.source_url if definition else "not found")

tasks = load_benchmark("humaneval", limit=5, language="python")
for task in tasks:
    print(task.task_id, task.prompt[:80])

load_benchmark() accepts:

Argument Default Meaning benchmark_id required Registry identifier limit None Maximum returned tasks language None Filter loaded tasks by language difficulty None Filter loaded tasks by difficulty force_refresh False Bypass the loader's existing cache

Benchmark loading requires the repository's agentic-tools package and may require network access. The package declares agentic-tools as a dependency, but the import is delayed until a dataset function is called.

Treat benchmark licenses, prompts, tests, and upstream revisions as part of the evaluation evidence. Record the benchmark ID, source revision when available, filters, and sample count with any published result.

docs.title: Local dataset format
docs.text:
The runtime server accepts a top-level JSON list or a JSON object containing one of these list fields:

  • tasks
  • samples
  • items

Example:

{
  "samples": [
    {
      "id": "sum-001",
      "input": {
        "feature_spec": "Return the sum of two integers"
      },
      "expected_output": "A tested implementation that returns a + b"
    }
  ]
}

The exact input keys must match the selected workflow. A dataset record may contain more metadata, but evaluation code should not assume optional fields exist.

The server discovers local JSON files under:

  • agentic-workflows-v2/tests/fixtures/datasets/
  • agentic-workflows-v2/evaluation/datasets/
  • tools/agents/benchmarks/gold_standards/

Tenant-aware deployments can further restrict local dataset visibility.

docs.title: Server API
docs.text:
The dashboard uses these routes:

Method Route Purpose GET /api/eval/datasets List repository datasets, local datasets, and configured evaluation sets GET /api/workflows/{workflow_name}/preview-dataset-inputs Preview how one sample maps to workflow inputs GET /api/eval/datasets/{source}/{dataset_id}/samples Return a page of sample summaries GET /api/eval/datasets/{source}/{dataset_id}/samples/{sample_index} Return one sample

The source is normally repository or local. Dataset IDs in path-based routes are URL encoded by the UI.

The older query-based sample routes remain for compatibility but are deprecated. New clients should use the path-based routes in the table.

See REST endpoints for the complete route map and authentication behavior.

docs.title: Workflow compatibility
docs.text:
When /api/eval/datasets receives a workflow filter, the server compares the workflow's required inputs with a representative dataset sample. This is a discovery aid, not a full validation of every row.

Before a long evaluation:

  1. Load the intended workflow.
  2. Inspect at least one complete dataset sample.
  3. Validate every required workflow input across all selected rows.
  4. Record skipped or malformed rows.
  5. Keep the dataset revision and evaluation configuration with the results.

docs.title: Safety
docs.text:
Benchmark tasks and local datasets are untrusted input. They can contain code, instructions, URLs, or text intended to change model behavior.

  • Do not execute generated code outside an appropriate sandbox.
  • Do not put credentials in dataset files.
  • Review licensing before redistributing dataset content.
  • Restrict network and file access for workflows that process external tasks.
  • Do not treat a benchmark score as evidence for an unrelated production use.

docs.title: Runtime evaluation gates
docs.text:
Runtime evaluation turns a completed workflow result into a score, grade, and pass/fail decision. It is separate from the agentic-v2-eval CLI, which scores numeric JSON values with a package rubric.

The implementation is in agentic-workflows-v2/agentic_v2/scoring/evaluation_scoring.py.

docs.title: When evaluation runs
docs.text:
The server can evaluate:

  • a workflow run requested with dataset-backed evaluation settings; or
  • a saved run through POST /api/runs/{filename}/evaluate.

Read a saved result with:

GET /api/runs/{filename}/evaluation

The evaluation is stored in the run record under extra.evaluation.

docs.title: Decision order
docs.text:
The runtime:

  1. resolves the rubric ID, weights, criteria, and scoring profile;
  2. calculates objective criterion scores from the workflow result and expected data;
  3. calculates advisory similarity and efficiency signals;
  4. optionally calls the runtime LLMJudge;
  5. combines the available layers into a 0–100 weighted score;
  6. assigns a letter grade;
  7. applies criterion floors; and
  8. applies hard gates and the pass threshold.

The default pass threshold is 70.0.

docs.title: Hard gates
docs.text:
Gate Pass condition required_outputs_present Every required workflow output resolves to a usable value overall_status_success The workflow result status is SUCCESS no_critical_step_failures No step result has status FAILED release_build_verified Any recognized release-build step succeeded and did not report a false readiness value schema_contract_valid The evaluation payload has the required fields and types dataset_workflow_compatible The selected sample provides inputs compatible with the workflow

When enforce_hard_gates=True, any failed hard gate:

  • sets the grade to F; and
  • makes passed false regardless of the weighted score.

The release-build gate passes when a workflow has no recognized release-build step.

docs.title: Criterion floors
docs.text:
A workflow criterion may declare a critical_floor:

evaluation:
  rubric_id: code_review_v1
  criteria:
    - name: correctness_rubric
      definition: Required behavior is correct.
      weight: 0.50
      critical_floor: 0.70
      formula_id: zero_one

A score below a required floor:

  • appears in floor_violations;
  • prevents the evaluation from passing; and
  • caps an otherwise passing letter grade at D.

Floors prevent a strong aggregate from hiding failure in one required dimension.

docs.title: Rubric resolution
docs.text:
Weights are resolved from lowest to highest priority:

  1. evaluation.scoring.weights in the runtime evaluation configuration;
  2. the workflow's named scoring profile;
  3. weight on each inline workflow criterion; and
  4. the workflow's explicit evaluation.weights mapping.

If a workflow declares criteria, inherited weights for undeclared criteria are removed. Resolved weights must be positive and sum to approximately 1.0.

The built-in fallback weights are:

Criterion Weight correctness 0.50 code_quality 0.25 efficiency 0.15 documentation 0.10

Do not compare results from different rubric versions, weight sets, or efficiency SLO bands as though they used the same scale.

docs.title: Optional judge
docs.text:
The judge is optional by default. If it is absent or fails, the payload records judge_skipped, judge_skip_reason, and judge_skip_code.

Set this configuration when evaluation must fail rather than continue without a judge:

evaluation:
  scoring:
    judge_required: true

With judge_required: true, an unavailable or failed judge raises JudgeRequiredError. The workflow run is still recorded, and the server maps the evaluation policy failure to HTTP 422.

See model-backed judges for calibration and interpretation.

docs.title: Pass logic
docs.text:
With hard-gate enforcement enabled:

passed =
  weighted_score >= pass_threshold
  and no criterion floor violations
  and all hard gates passed

Disabling hard-gate enforcement removes only the final hard-gate condition. Criterion floors and the score threshold still apply.

docs.title: Result fields
docs.text:
The evaluation payload includes:

  • rubric ID and version;
  • criterion scores and weights;
  • objective, advisory, and judge layer details;
  • weighted score and overall score;
  • grade and whether it was capped;
  • pass threshold and final passed value;
  • hard-gate results and failures;
  • criterion floor violations; and
  • judge metadata or the reason the judge was skipped.

Use the structured fields when building automation. Do not parse display text.

docs.title: Release use
docs.text:
Before using an evaluation as a release gate:

  1. Fix the workflow, dataset, rubric, provider, judge prompt, and model versions.
  2. Validate the threshold against representative accepted and rejected cases.
  3. Exercise every hard-gate failure.
  4. Make judge failure policy explicit.
  5. Store the full payload, not only the final score.
  6. Require human review for high-impact decisions.

For simple numeric file scoring in CI, use the evaluation package's --fail-under option instead:

agentic-v2-eval evaluate .\results.json --fail-under 0.80

docs.title: Model-backed judges
docs.text:
A model-backed judge asks one model to score another output. It can make review cheaper and repeatable, but it does not turn a subjective model response into ground truth.

The repository contains two separate judge systems:

System Location Purpose Runtime LLMJudge agentic_v2/scoring/judge.py Score a workflow result against anchored criteria Evaluation-package evaluators agentic_v2_eval/evaluators/ Score choices, quality dimensions, prompts, and named reasoning patterns

The agentic-v2-eval evaluate CLI does not call these judges. That command applies a numeric YAML rubric to values already present in a JSON file.

docs.title: Runtime judge
docs.text:
LLMJudge accepts:

  • a candidate output;
  • an optional expected output;
  • one or more criteria with names, definitions, and 1–5 anchors; and
  • an optional second candidate for an order-consistency check.

It requires a configured runtime model client or an injected response_provider.

from agentic_v2.scoring.judge import LLMJudge

def fixed_response(**_):
    return {
        "criteria": [
            {
                "name": "correctness",
                "score": 4,
                "evidence": "The required behavior is present.",
            }
        ]
    }

judge = LLMJudge(
    model="test:fixed",
    model_version="fixed-1",
    response_provider=fixed_response,
)

result = judge.evaluate(
    candidate_output="The implementation returns a sorted copy.",
    expected_output="Return a sorted copy without changing the input.",
    criteria=[
        {
            "name": "correctness",
            "definition": "Does the output meet the requirement?",
            "scale": {
                "1": "Does not meet it",
                "3": "Partly meets it",
                "5": "Fully meets it",
            },
        }
    ],
)

print(result.normalized_score)

The judge:

  1. shuffles criterion order from a stable seed;
  2. requests strict JSON;
  3. rejects missing, duplicate, unexpected, or out-of-range criterion results;
  4. normalizes 1–5 scores to 0.0–1.0; and
  5. returns the mean normalized score.

When pairwise_reference_output is supplied, the judge evaluates both presentation orders. It reports criteria whose raw scores differ by more than the configured consistency tolerance. This checks order sensitivity; it does not prove either candidate is correct.

The result records the judge model, model version, prompt version, temperature, criterion evidence, and pairwise consistency fields.

docs.title: Evaluation-package judges
docs.text: All evaluation-package judges receive an injected client that implements generate_text(...). Provider setup stays outside the package.

docs.title: LLMEvaluator
docs.text:
LLMEvaluator maps a judge response to caller-defined choices:

from agentic_v2_eval.evaluators import (
    LLMEvaluator,
    STANDARD_CHOICES,
)

class FixedClient:
    def generate_text(self, **_):
        return "4"

evaluator = LLMEvaluator(
    model_id="test:fixed",
    system_prompt="Score the response from 1 to 5.",
    prompt_template="Response:\n{{completion}}\n\nScore:",
    choices=STANDARD_CHOICES,
    llm_client=FixedClient(),
    seed=0,
)

result = evaluator.evaluate("A complete response")
print(result["score"])  # 0.75

The built-in choices map 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 to 0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, and 1.0. Choice matching checks the last lines of the response. Write prompts that require only the choice label on the final line.

docs.title: QualityEvaluator
docs.text:
QualityEvaluator loads five definitions from quality.yaml:

  • COHERENCE
  • FLUENCY
  • RELEVANCE
  • GROUNDEDNESS
  • SIMILARITY

Call evaluate(definition, inputs, output, model_override=None). It returns a single normalized float. A provider or parse failure returns 0.0, so preserve logs if you need to distinguish a failed judge call from a low score.

docs.title: StandardEvaluator
docs.text:
StandardEvaluator.score_prompt() evaluates prompt clarity, effectiveness, structure, specificity, and completeness. It returns StandardScore on a 0–10 scale.

score = evaluator.score_prompt(
    prompt_name="reviewer",
    prompt_content=prompt_text,
    model="gh:gpt-4o",
    runs=1,
    temperature=0.1,
)

The default is one run. When runs is greater than one, the evaluator takes the median for each dimension.

docs.title: PatternEvaluator
docs.text:
PatternEvaluator.score_pattern() checks one of the patterns defined in prompt_pattern.yaml: react, cove, reflexion, or rag.

It returns a PatternScore containing universal scores, pattern-specific scores, hard-gate results, parse success counts, and judge metadata. The default is one run.

docs.title: Using judge scores responsibly
docs.text:
• Keep the judge prompt and model version with the result.
  • Calibrate against human-scored examples from the intended domain.
  • Use more than one run when score variance matters.
  • Test position, verbosity, and style bias.
  • Treat parse failures and provider failures separately from low-quality answers.
  • Do not use a judge score as the only approval for a high-impact action.
  • Do not claim the judge exposes or audits a model's private reasoning.

The runtime server exposes recorded evaluation data at GET /api/runs/{filename}/evaluation. See production gating for how runtime scores become pass or fail decisions.

docs.title: Rubrics
docs.text:
A scoring rubric names the values expected in a result and assigns a weight to each value. Scorer normalizes each supplied value to 0.0–1.0, applies the weights, and returns a weighted score.

Rubric names and result keys are case-sensitive.

docs.title: Bundled files
docs.text:
The package currently ships eight YAML files:

Rubric Contents Used by default Accuracy, Completeness, Efficiency Scorer and the CLI default agent Six agent-output criteria Scorer code Five code-output criteria Scorer coding_standards Eight repository coding-standard criteria Scorer pattern Six pattern-execution criteria and hard-gate metadata Scorer or custom gates quality Prompt templates for five quality definitions QualityEvaluator prompt_standard Prompt template for five-dimension prompt review StandardEvaluator prompt_pattern Prompt templates and rules for named agentic patterns PatternEvaluator

Only files with a criteria list can be passed directly to Scorer. quality, prompt_standard, and prompt_pattern configure model-backed evaluators instead.

List and load the current files at runtime:

from agentic_v2_eval.rubrics import list_rubrics, load_rubric

print(list_rubrics())
rubric = load_rubric("agent")

docs.title: Scoring
docs.text:
from agentic_v2_eval import Scorer
from agentic_v2_eval.rubrics import load_rubric

scorer = Scorer(load_rubric("default"))
result = scorer.score(
    {
        "Accuracy": 0.90,
        "Completeness": 0.80,
        "Efficiency": 0.75,
    }
)

print(result.weighted_score)
print(result.total_score)
print(result.criterion_scores)
print(result.missing_criteria)

The returned fields mean:

Field Meaning weighted_score Weighted aggregate across all rubric criteria total_score Unweighted mean across all rubric criteria criterion_scores Supplied values after clamping missing_criteria Rubric criteria absent from the result

Missing criteria receive no points while their weight remains in the denominator. This lowers both aggregate scores.

docs.title: Normalization
docs.text:
Each criterion may define:

- name: Correctness
  description: The result satisfies the stated requirements.
  weight: 0.7
  min_value: 0
  max_value: 10

Scorer:

  1. converts the supplied value to float;
  2. clamps it to the configured range;
  3. normalizes it with (value - min_value) / (max_value - min_value); and
  4. applies the criterion weight.

If min_value and max_value are omitted, they default to 0.0 and 1.0.

The scorer divides by the sum of the configured weights. Weights do not need to sum to 1.0, although normalized weights are easier to review.

docs.title: Thresholds
docs.text:
Some bundled scoring rubrics contain thresholds metadata such as:

thresholds:
  pass: 0.70
  excellent: 0.90
  warning: 0.50

Scorer.score() does not apply these thresholds. A caller must compare weighted_score with the intended threshold, or use the CLI's explicit --fail-under option.

agentic-v2-eval evaluate .\results.json --fail-under 0.80

The command exits with code 2 when the average weighted score is below the requested threshold.

docs.title: Custom rubric
docs.text:
name: Release review
version: "1.0"
criteria:
  - name: Correctness
    description: Required behavior is present and tested.
    weight: 0.6
    min_value: 0
    max_value: 1

  - name: Safety
    description: Required security and failure controls are present.
    weight: 0.4
    min_value: 0
    max_value: 1

Use it from Python:

from agentic_v2_eval import Scorer

scorer = Scorer("release-rubric.yaml")

Or from the command line:

agentic-v2-eval evaluate .\results.json `
  --rubric .\release-rubric.yaml `
  --output .\scored.json

Before using a rubric as a release gate:

  • define how each raw value is produced;
  • keep criterion names identical across producers and the rubric;
  • test missing, invalid, minimum, and maximum values;
  • choose a threshold from representative data rather than intuition; and
  • store the rubric revision with the evaluation result.

docs.title: Evaluation runners
docs.text: An evaluation runner applies a caller-supplied function to a collection of test cases. Runners handle iteration, progress, and errors. They do not choose a rubric or decide whether a score passes.

docs.title: Choose a runner
docs.text:
Runner Evaluator type Result delivery Concurrency BatchRunner Synchronous One BatchResult after all cases Sequential StreamingRunner Synchronous Callback or iterator as cases finish Sequential AsyncStreamingRunner Synchronous or asynchronous Async iterator as cases finish Bounded; default 5

BatchRunner and StreamingRunner are exported from agentic_v2_eval.runners. AsyncStreamingRunner currently requires a direct import from agentic_v2_eval.runners.streaming.

docs.title: Batch runner
docs.text:
from agentic_v2_eval.runners import BatchRunner

cases = [
    {"actual": "A", "expected": "A"},
    {"actual": "B", "expected": "C"},
]

def evaluate_case(case: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, bool]:
    return {"matches": case["actual"] == case["expected"]}

runner = BatchRunner(
    evaluator=evaluate_case,
    on_progress=lambda current, total: print(f"{current}/{total}"),
)
batch = runner.run(cases)

print(batch.results)
print(batch.errors)
print(batch.success_rate)

BatchResult contains:

Field Meaning results Successful evaluator return values errors (case_index, exception) pairs total Submitted cases successful Calls that returned without an exception failed Calls that raised success_rate successful / total

success_rate measures runner completion. It does not measure answer quality.

The constructor accepts:

BatchRunner(
    evaluator,
    on_progress=None,
    on_error=None,
    continue_on_error=True,
)

With continue_on_error=False, the first evaluator exception is raised.

For a result list without statistics, use:

from agentic_v2_eval.runners import run_batch_evaluation

results = run_batch_evaluation(cases, evaluate_case)

docs.title: Synchronous streaming runner
docs.text:
Use StreamingRunner when the input may be an iterator or the caller should receive each result immediately:

from agentic_v2_eval.runners import StreamingRunner

runner = StreamingRunner(
    evaluator=evaluate_case,
    on_result=lambda result: print(result),
    on_error=lambda case, error: print(case, error),
)

stats = runner.run(cases)
print(stats.processed, stats.successful, stats.failed)

To consume results as an iterator:

for result in runner.iter_results(cases):
    print(result)

iter_results() yields successful results. It logs and skips evaluator errors when continue_on_error=True.

docs.title: Asynchronous streaming runner
docs.text:
Use the async runner for network-bound evaluators when concurrent calls are safe:

import asyncio

from agentic_v2_eval.runners.streaming import AsyncStreamingRunner

async def evaluate_remote(case: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    return {"id": case["id"], "score": "complete"}

async def main() -> None:
    runner = AsyncStreamingRunner(
        evaluator=evaluate_remote,
        max_concurrency=4,
    )
    async for result in runner.iter_results(
        [{"id": "a"}, {"id": "b"}, {"id": "c"}]
    ):
        print(result)

asyncio.run(main())

The runner accepts a normal iterable or an async iterable. Results are yielded in completion order, which may differ from input order.

docs.title: Error behavior
docs.text:
• continue_on_error=True records or skips a failed case and continues.
  • continue_on_error=False raises the first observed evaluator exception.
  • Callbacks run in the same process as the evaluator. Keep them fast and avoid modifying shared state without synchronization.
  • A process interruption can leave a partial result set. Persist results in an on_result callback when partial recovery matters.

docs.title: Reporting results
docs.text:
Reporters accept a list of dictionaries:

from agentic_v2_eval.reporters import MarkdownReporter

MarkdownReporter().generate(batch.results, "evaluation-report.md")

If an evaluator returns dataclasses such as StandardScore or PatternScore, call to_dict() before passing them to a reporter.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
The CLI scores existing JSON data; it does not expose these runner classes:

agentic-v2-eval evaluate .\results.json --output .\scored.json
agentic-v2-eval report .\scored.json --format html --output .\report.html

See the evaluation package README for the input format and exit codes.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: Choose the path that matches the work you want to do.

docs.title: Run an existing workflow
docs.text:
Start with the quick start if you want to verify the runtime without provider credentials. You will:

  1. install the workspace;
  2. create a JSON input file;
  3. run the deterministic workflow; and
  4. inspect the result.

AGENTIC_NO_LLM=1 is available when you want to run an LLM-backed workflow without making provider calls. It returns fixed placeholder text, so it checks control flow rather than model quality.

docs.title: Write a workflow
docs.text:
Start with your first workflow if you want to define steps, dependencies, inputs, and outputs in YAML. Continue with:

  • Workflow authoring for the full schema;
  • Workflow reference for the shipped definitions; and
  • Pattern catalog for branching, fan-in, loops, and review patterns.

docs.title: Run the server and dashboard
docs.text:
Start with installation, then run:

just dev

The development launcher starts:

  • FastAPI on http://127.0.0.1:8010;
  • Vite on http://127.0.0.1:5173; and
  • the UI proxy from /api and /ws to the backend.

Use just dev-status to inspect the processes and just dev-stop to stop them.

docs.title: Integrate the platform
docs.text:
Read these pages before connecting the runtime to another system:

Need Reference CLI commands and exit behavior CLI reference HTTP, SSE, and WebSocket routes API contracts Environment variables Configuration Runtime and package boundaries Architecture Runnable Python examples for engines, cost caps, approvals, and scoring Integration recipes Authentication and tool controls Security hardening Deployment gaps and workarounds Known limitations

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.11 or newer
  • Node.js 22.22.2 or newer for the dashboard (CI uses Node 22)
  • npm
  • Git
  • just for the repository shortcuts, or the ability to run the equivalent commands manually

Docker and provider credentials are not required for the deterministic workflow. A real model-backed run needs the package extra and credential for the provider path you select.

docs.title: Useful checks
docs.text:
agentic version
agentic list workflows
agentic list adapters
agentic validate test_deterministic

If a command fails, use the troubleshooting guide and check known limitations before opening an issue.

docs.title: Integration recipes
docs.text:
Each recipe uses the public Python surface and runs without a provider credential unless it says otherwise. Run them from an environment installed with just setup or the manual steps, which include the langchain extra, and set AGENTIC_NO_LLM=1 so nothing can reach a provider.

If you install pieces by hand, install the root tools package first and pass the constraints file to every install:

python -m pip install -e . -c ci-constraints.txt
python -m pip install -e "./agentic-workflows-v2[langchain]" -c ci-constraints.txt

Without the langchain extra the LangChain adapter is not registered and list_adapters() returns only ['native'].

docs.title: 1. Run a workflow on either execution engine
docs.text:
Both engines are reached through the AdapterRegistry. A named YAML workflow loads and runs the same way on each of them:

import asyncio

from agentic_v2.adapters import get_registry


async def main() -> None:
    registry = get_registry()
    print("adapters:", registry.list_adapters())
    for name in ("native", "langchain"):
        engine = registry.get_adapter(name)
        workflow = engine.load_workflow("test_deterministic")
        result = await engine.execute(
            workflow, workflow_inputs={"input_text": "Hello World"}
        )
        print(name, result.overall_status.value, result.final_output)


asyncio.run(main())

Both lines report success with the same processed_text and step_count. The command-line equivalent is agentic compare test_deterministic --input in.json --adapters native,langchain; see the CLI reference.

A runtime-built DAG is different: only the native engine accepts it. LangChainEngine takes a workflow name, a path, or a LangChain WorkflowConfig and raises TypeError for a DAG, and NativeEngine raises TypeError for a bare workflow name. Step functions are async, and what a step returns lands under that step's outputs unless output_mapping copies it into a context variable for later steps:

import asyncio

from agentic_v2.adapters import get_registry
from agentic_v2.engine import DAG, ExecutionContext, StepDefinition


async def ingest(ctx: ExecutionContext) -> dict[str, str]:
    return {"cleaned": ctx.get_sync("raw").strip().upper()}


async def count(ctx: ExecutionContext) -> dict[str, int]:
    return {"length": len(ctx.get_sync("cleaned"))}


async def main() -> None:
    dag = DAG(name="adapter_demo")
    dag.add(
        StepDefinition(
            name="ingest", func=ingest, output_mapping={"cleaned": "cleaned"}
        )
    ).add(
        StepDefinition(
            name="count",
            func=count,
            depends_on=["ingest"],
            output_mapping={"length": "length"},
        )
    )
    ctx = ExecutionContext(variables={"raw": "  agentic runtime  "})
    result = await get_registry().get_adapter("native").execute(dag, ctx)
    print(result.overall_status.value, ctx.get_sync("cleaned"), ctx.get_sync("length"))


asyncio.run(main())

This prints success AGENTIC RUNTIME 15. See Runtime architecture for how the registry selects an engine.

docs.title: 2. Cap model cost with a cost-lane ceiling
docs.text:
AGENTIC_MAX_COST_LANE (local, free, or paid, the default) drops candidate models above the ceiling by their curated cost_lane in model_registry.yaml. An id missing from the registry counts as paid. The variable is read on every call, so set it in the process environment; the assignment below only keeps the example self-contained.

SmartModelRouter excludes over-ceiling models inside a tier and, when a tier has none left, degrades to another tier and records that on last_selection. It raises only when every tier is exhausted (and AGENTIC_NO_LLM is unset):

import os

from agentic_v2.models import FallbackChain, ModelTier, SmartModelRouter

os.environ["AGENTIC_MAX_COST_LANE"] = "free"

router = SmartModelRouter()
router.register_chain(
    ModelTier.TIER_2,
    FallbackChain.build("lane")
    .add("anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6")  # paid: excluded by the ceiling
    .add("ollama:qwen3-coder:30b")  # local: allowed
    .done(),
)
print(router.get_model_for_tier(ModelTier.TIER_2), router.last_selection)

# A tier whose whole chain is above the ceiling degrades to another tier.
router.register_chain(
    ModelTier.TIER_4,
    FallbackChain(("anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6",), name="paid-only"),
)
print(router.get_model_for_tier(ModelTier.TIER_4), router.last_selection)

The first selection is TIER_2 with is_degraded=False; the second reports requested_tier='TIER_4', actual_tier='TIER_3', and is_degraded=True.

The simpler ModelRouter, and the LangChain model builder, behave differently: when the ceiling filters out every candidate they refuse instead of degrading, raising CostLaneCeilingExceededError:

import os

from agentic_v2.models import FallbackChain, ModelRouter, ModelTier
from agentic_v2.models.model_registry import CostLaneCeilingExceededError

os.environ["AGENTIC_MAX_COST_LANE"] = "free"

router = ModelRouter()
router.register_chain(
    ModelTier.TIER_4, FallbackChain(("anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6",), name="paid-only")
)
try:
    router.get_model_for_tier(ModelTier.TIER_4)
except CostLaneCeilingExceededError as exc:
    print("refused:", exc)

Tiers run from TIER_0 (deterministic, no model) to TIER_5. Mistral and DigitalOcean model ids are served only by the LangChain engine; the native backend fails loudly for them. See Configuration and ADR-059.

docs.title: 3. Wire tool approval
docs.text:
Every tool call that needs approval goes through evaluate_tool_approval(). A call needs approval when the tool sets requires_approval (the high-impact built-ins such as file_write), when AGENTIC_REQUIRE_TOOL_APPROVAL is on (every tool), or when its name is listed in AGENTIC_APPROVAL_REQUIRED_TOOLS. Read-only tools such as file_read are not gated by default.

With no provider registered, a gated call is denied (fail-closed). AutoDenyProvider is a separate, explicit kill switch and is never installed for you:

import asyncio

from agentic_v2.governance import (
    ApprovalDecision,
    ApprovalRequest,
    CallbackApprovalProvider,
    PolicyApprovalProvider,
    evaluate_tool_approval,
    set_approval_provider,
)
from agentic_v2.tools.builtin import FileReadTool, FileWriteTool


async def check(tool, name: str, label: str) -> None:
    outcome = await evaluate_tool_approval(
        tool, name, {"path": "notes.txt"}, call_id="c1", agent_or_step="demo"
    )
    print(f"{label:<28} allowed={outcome.allowed} via {outcome.provider_label}")


async def main() -> None:
    write, read = FileWriteTool(), FileReadTool()

    await check(write, "file_write", "no provider, gated tool")
    await check(read, "file_read", "no provider, read-only tool")

    set_approval_provider(PolicyApprovalProvider(frozenset({"file_write"})))
    await check(write, "file_write", "allowlisted tool")

    def operator_prompt(request: ApprovalRequest) -> ApprovalDecision:
        print("  asked to approve:", request.tool_name)
        return ApprovalDecision.DENIED

    set_approval_provider(CallbackApprovalProvider(operator_prompt))
    await check(write, "file_write", "callback provider")

    set_approval_provider(None)


asyncio.run(main())

The first line is denied via no provider registered, the read-only tool is not-required, the allowlisted tool is approved, and the callback decides for itself. The callback may also be async, which is the hook for an interactive prompt or a remote approval service. Register a provider once at process start. The structural gate itself (BaseTool.__init_subclass__) needs no extra install; see ADR-041, ADR-047, and Known limitations section 4.3.

docs.title: ExecutionKit delegation (ek extra)
docs.text:
Separately from the gate, the optional ek extra routes model calls through the ExecutionKit-backed provider:

python -m pip install -e "./agentic-workflows-v2[ek]" -c ci-constraints.txt

With the package installed, AGENTIC_EK_PROVIDER defaults to 1 and ordinary get_client().complete(...) calls and LLM steps use it automatically; set AGENTIC_EK_PROVIDER=0 to roll back to the legacy path. To observe each physical attempt, build the provider yourself and pass an attempt_callback (each ProviderAttempt records model, latency_ms, ok, error_type, and streaming):

import asyncio

from agentic_v2.models import MockBackend, ModelTier, SmartModelRouter
from agentic_v2.models.ek_provider import ProviderAttempt, SmartRouterProvider


async def main() -> None:
    attempts: list[ProviderAttempt] = []
    provider = SmartRouterProvider(
        SmartModelRouter(),
        MockBackend(default_response="hello"),
        ModelTier.TIER_2,
        attempt_callback=attempts.append,
    )
    response = await provider.complete([{"role": "user", "content": "Say hi"}])
    print(response.content, attempts)


asyncio.run(main())

See ADR-023.

docs.title: 4. Use Claude through a subscription sign-in (claude extra)
docs.text:
This recipe needs the claude extra and a signed-in Claude Code, so it does not run in a key-free environment:

python -m pip install -e "./agentic-workflows-v2[claude]" -c ci-constraints.txt

ClaudeSDKAgent wraps the Claude Agent SDK. It is not a BaseAgent and bypasses the tool registry; the SDK's own tools (Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, ...) do the work:

import asyncio

from agentic_v2.agents.implementations import ClaudeSDKAgent


async def main() -> None:
    agent = ClaudeSDKAgent(tools=["Read", "Glob", "Grep"], cwd=".")
    print(await agent.run("List the top-level directories in one line each."))


asyncio.run(main())

To use the same sign-in as a model backend, use an id with the claude: prefix. The backend registers itself when the SDK is importable. The child process has ANTHROPIC_API_KEY blanked so the subscription, not an API key, is billed (ADR-058). See Agents deep dive.

docs.title: 5. Score output against a rubric
docs.text:
CriterionScorer is the key-free weighted scorer and needs no extra. Weights live in the rubric:

from agentic_v2.scoring.criterion_aggregation import CriterionScorer

rubric = {
    "criteria": [
        {"name": "correctness", "weight": 0.5},
        {"name": "completeness", "weight": 0.3},
        {"name": "safety", "weight": 0.2},
    ]
}
scorer = CriterionScorer(rubric)

full = scorer.score({"correctness": 0.92, "completeness": 0.85, "safety": 1.0})
print(round(full.weighted_score, 4), full.missing_criteria)

partial = scorer.score({"correctness": 0.92, "completeness": 0.85})
print(round(partial.weighted_score, 4), partial.missing_criteria)

This prints 0.915 () and then 0.715 ('safety',): a missing criterion keeps its weight in the denominator, so it lowers the score and is listed in missing_criteria.

With the eval extra (agentic-evalkit, see ADR-042), the evalkit bridge scores the same input and returns 0.915:

from agentic_v2.scoring import evalkit_bridge

print(evalkit_bridge.EVALKIT_AVAILABLE)
print(
    evalkit_bridge.score_criteria(
        rubric, {"correctness": 0.92, "completeness": 0.85, "safety": 1.0}
    )
)

The 0.80 figure is not a general pass mark. It is the --threshold the golden-dataset gate in CI uses, and you can run that gate locally from the repository root:

AGENTIC_NO_LLM=1 python scripts/eval_gate.py \
  --cases datasets/default/golden_cases.json --threshold 0.80

The runtime scorer's own default pass threshold is 70.0 on a 0-100 scale; see Gating.

docs.title: First workflow
docs.text: This guide creates a two-step workflow that runs without a model. It uses the same tier-0 agents as the repository's deterministic smoke test, so you can focus on the YAML contract.

docs.title: 1. Create the definition
docs.text:
Save this file as my-first-workflow.yaml in the repository root:

name: my_first_workflow
description: Process text and count the result
version: "1.0"

inputs:
  input_text:
    type: string
    description: Text to process
    required: true

outputs:
  processed_text:
    from: ${steps.process.outputs.result}
  character_count:
    from: ${steps.count.outputs.count}

steps:
  - name: process
    agent: tier0_process
    description: Process the input text
    inputs:
      text: ${inputs.input_text}
    outputs:
      result: processed_text

  - name: count
    agent: tier0_counter
    description: Count characters in the processed text
    depends_on: [process]
    inputs:
      text: ${steps.process.outputs.result}
    outputs:
      count: count_value

The top-level sections have distinct jobs:

Section Meaning name, description, version Workflow identity and human-readable context inputs Values callers may or must supply outputs Values returned from the completed workflow steps Work to execute and the dependencies between steps

Each step has a unique name and an agent. depends_on creates a graph edge. Here, count cannot run until process succeeds.

Expressions connect values:

  • ${inputs.input_text} reads a workflow input.
  • ${steps.process.outputs.result} reads an earlier step output.
  • top-level outputs select the values returned in final_output.

The mapping under a step's outputs declares the public output name and its internal context alias. Downstream expressions use the public name on the left.

docs.title: 2. Validate
docs.text:
agentic validate ./my-first-workflow.yaml --verbose

Validation checks:

  • YAML syntax;
  • required workflow fields;
  • duplicate or missing step names;
  • dependency references;
  • cycles; and
  • LangGraph compilation.

The final compilation check requires the langchain extra even if you later run with --adapter native.

Expected result:

OK Workflow 'my_first_workflow' is valid!

docs.title: 3. Create an input file
docs.text:
Bash:

printf '{"input_text":"hello"}\n' > /tmp/my-first-input.json

PowerShell:

'{"input_text":"hello"}' |
  Set-Content -Encoding ascii .\my-first-input.json

docs.title: 4. Run
docs.text:
Bash:

AGENTIC_NO_LLM=1 agentic run ./my-first-workflow.yaml \
  --input /tmp/my-first-input.json \
  --verbose

PowerShell:

$env:AGENTIC_NO_LLM = "1"
agentic run .\my-first-workflow.yaml `
  --input .\my-first-input.json `
  --verbose

Expected status:

Status: SUCCESS

The resolved output should contain the processed text and its character count. Save the full result when you want to inspect the contract:

agentic run ./my-first-workflow.yaml \
  --input /tmp/my-first-input.json \
  --output my-first-result.json

docs.title: 5. Run through the native engine
docs.text:
The default named-workflow adapter is LangGraph. Select the native engine explicitly:

agentic run ./my-first-workflow.yaml \
  --input /tmp/my-first-input.json \
  --adapter native

For this simple workflow, both adapters should return the same output.

docs.title: 6. Add a parallel branch
docs.text:
Steps with the same satisfied dependencies are eligible to run at the same time. Add this step after count:

  - name: second_count
    agent: tier0_counter
    description: Independently count the original input
    inputs:
      text: ${inputs.input_text}
    outputs:
      count: original_count

second_count has no dependency, so it can run at the same time as process. Add its result to the top-level outputs:

outputs:
  processed_text:
    from: ${steps.process.outputs.result}
  character_count:
    from: ${steps.count.outputs.count}
  original_character_count:
    from: ${steps.second_count.outputs.count}

Validate again after every graph change:

agentic validate ./my-first-workflow.yaml --verbose

docs.title: Input is missing
docs.text: agentic validate does not read your input file. If the input JSON omits input_text, agentic run rejects it with an input-validation error before any step executes. Compare the file with the top-level inputs block.

docs.title: Dependency name is wrong
docs.text: depends_on uses step names, not agent names. A dependency such as depends_on: [tier0_process] is invalid unless a step is actually named tier0_process.

docs.title: Output cannot be resolved
docs.text:
Check all three names:

  1. the producer step name;
  2. the step's public output name; and
  3. the top-level from expression.

An expression for this file must use ${steps.process.outputs.result}, not the internal alias processed_text.

docs.title: LLM-backed step returns placeholder text
docs.text: Tier-1 and higher agents call a model. Under AGENTIC_NO_LLM=1, they receive fixed placeholder text. That text may not satisfy JSON or typed-artifact contracts. Use tier-0 steps while learning the graph, then configure a real provider before testing model-dependent output.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
The repository contains three Python packages and one Node application:

Path Package Purpose repository root agentic-tools Shared model and benchmark utilities agentic-workflows-v2/ agentic-workflows-v2 Runtime, CLI, and server agentic-v2-eval/ agentic-v2-eval Rubrics, evaluators, runners, and reporters agentic-workflows-v2/ui/ private npm package React dashboard

Use Python 3.11 or newer and Node.js 22.22.2 or newer (CI uses Node 22).

docs.title: Full development setup
docs.text:
Clone the repository:

git clone https://github.com/tafreeman/agentic-runtime-platform.git
cd agentic-runtime-platform

On Windows, the repository shortcut creates .venv, installs all Python packages, and installs the UI dependencies:

just setup

just setup installs into .venv but does not activate it in your shell. Activate it before using the agentic command:

.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

The current justfile selects powershell.exe. Use the manual setup below on Linux or macOS.

Verify the installation:

agentic version
agentic list workflows
npm --prefix agentic-workflows-v2/ui run build

docs.title: Manual setup
docs.text: Run these commands from the repository root.

docs.title: Bash
docs.text:
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install -e . -c ci-constraints.txt
python -m pip install \
  -e "./agentic-workflows-v2[dev,server,langchain,tracing]" \
  -c ci-constraints.txt
python -m pip install -e "./agentic-v2-eval[dev]" -c ci-constraints.txt
npm --prefix agentic-workflows-v2/ui install

docs.title: PowerShell
docs.text:
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install -e . -c ci-constraints.txt
python -m pip install `
  -e "./agentic-workflows-v2[dev,server,langchain,tracing]" `
  -c ci-constraints.txt
python -m pip install -e "./agentic-v2-eval[dev]" -c ci-constraints.txt
npm --prefix agentic-workflows-v2/ui install

Installing the root package first matters: both child packages resolve shared code through the workspace's agentic-tools package.

ci-constraints.txt is generated from uv.lock. Using it keeps local dependency versions aligned with CI.

docs.title: Runtime extras
docs.text:
Extras are declared in agentic-workflows-v2/pyproject.toml.

Extra Use it for dev pytest, coverage, Ruff, Black, mypy, test fakes, and schema tools server FastAPI, Uvicorn, multipart uploads, rate limiting, and JWT verification langchain The default adapter for named YAML workflows and LangGraph compilation during validation tracing OpenTelemetry SDK, OTLP exporters, Prometheus exporter, and client ek ExecutionKit integration eval The agentic-evalkit scoring bridge (ADR-042) swe-ab pandas, used to build SWE-bench cases for agentic-workflows-v2/evals/swe_ab devex Process inspection used by development commands mcp WebSocket transport for the MCP client redis Redis-backed shared state and replay storage sqlite Async SQLite support postgres PostgreSQL LangGraph checkpointer claude Claude Agent SDK integration

Add extras to the same editable install:

python -m pip install \
  -e "./agentic-workflows-v2[dev,server,langchain,tracing,redis]" \
  -c ci-constraints.txt

Optional packages fail when their feature is selected, not when the base runtime is imported. For example, requesting the PostgreSQL checkpointer without the postgres extra raises an install hint.

docs.title: Deterministic verification
docs.text:
Create an input file:

printf '{"input_text":"hello"}\n' > /tmp/agentic-input.json
AGENTIC_NO_LLM=1 agentic run test_deterministic \
  --input /tmp/agentic-input.json

PowerShell:

'{"input_text":"hello"}' |
  Set-Content -Encoding ascii .\agentic-input.json
$env:AGENTIC_NO_LLM = "1"
agentic run test_deterministic --input .\agentic-input.json

Use -Encoding ascii here: Windows PowerShell 5.1 writes a byte-order mark with -Encoding utf8, which the CLI rejects. The repository also ships a ready-made input at agentic-workflows-v2/tests/fixtures/deterministic_input.json.

Expected result: Status: SUCCESS.

The deterministic workflow itself does not call a model. Setting AGENTIC_NO_LLM=1 also protects you if you continue with an LLM-backed workflow before configuring provider credentials.

docs.title: Provider configuration
docs.text:
Copy the environment template:

cp .env.example .env

PowerShell:

Copy-Item .env.example .env

Set only the providers you intend to use. Common chat-provider variables are:

Provider Main variable OpenAI OPENAI_API_KEY Anthropic ANTHROPIC_API_KEY Gemini GEMINI_API_KEY or GOOGLE_API_KEY Azure OpenAI AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY and AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT Azure AI Foundry AZURE_FOUNDRY_API_KEY and AZURE_FOUNDRY_ENDPOINT NVIDIA NIM NVIDIA_API_KEY, or NVIDIA_BASE_URL for a self-hosted endpoint OpenRouter OPENROUTER_API_KEY DigitalOcean Serverless Inference DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN Mistral La Plateforme MISTRAL_API_KEY GitHub Models GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN; retired upstream 2026-07-30, so no default tier routes to it Ollama OLLAMA_BASE_URL (runtime; OLLAMA_HOST is read by the inventory and benchmark tools); OLLAMA_API_KEY only when the endpoint requires it

See Configuration for model overrides, endpoint settings, authentication, storage, and security controls.

Do not commit .env or provider credentials.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
After installing the UI dependencies:

just dev

Or start the two processes manually.

Terminal 1:

agentic serve --port 8010 --dev --no-open

Terminal 2:

npm --prefix agentic-workflows-v2/ui run dev

Open http://127.0.0.1:5173. Vite proxies /api and /ws to http://127.0.0.1:8010.

Build the production UI:

npm --prefix agentic-workflows-v2/ui run build

When ui/dist exists, the FastAPI application can serve that build from the same origin as the API.

docs.title: PowerShell bootstrap
docs.text:
The runtime package also includes a Windows setup script:

.\agentic-workflows-v2\scripts\setup-dev.ps1

Run it from the repository root. Use -SkipFrontend to skip the UI and -SkipSmokeTest to skip its workflow smoke check.

docs.title: Evaluation package
docs.text:
The full setup installs the evaluation package. Verify its command:

agentic-v2-eval --help
python -m agentic_v2_eval --help

See Evaluation architecture and evaluation runners before supplying result files.

docs.title: Pre-commit hooks
docs.text:
Install the configured pre-commit and commit-message hooks:

pre-commit install --install-hooks
pre-commit run --all-files

The current hook configuration runs Black, Ruff with import sorting, docformatter, detect-secrets, and strict mypy for the evaluation package source. Pydocstyle is enforced on selected runtime modules in CI, not by the local hook.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: This walkthrough verifies the CLI, workflow discovery, input validation, dependency ordering, and result serialization. It does not need a provider credential.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
Requirements: Python 3.11+, Node.js 22.22.2+, and npm. CI uses Node 22. Node 20.19+ or 22.12+ is enough for npm run dev and npm run build, but the UI test dependencies (Vitest 5, jsdom 30) need Node 22.22.2+, 24.15+, or 26+.

Windows (PowerShell with just):

git clone https://github.com/tafreeman/agentic-runtime-platform.git
cd agentic-runtime-platform
just setup
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

just setup creates .venv and installs into it, but it does not activate the environment in your shell. Activate it as above, or call .\.venv\Scripts\agentic.exe explicitly.

Linux or macOS (the justfile uses PowerShell, so use the manual path):

git clone https://github.com/tafreeman/agentic-runtime-platform.git
cd agentic-runtime-platform
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install -e . -c ci-constraints.txt
python -m pip install \
  -e "./agentic-workflows-v2[dev,server,langchain,tracing]" \
  -c ci-constraints.txt
python -m pip install -e "./agentic-v2-eval[dev]" -c ci-constraints.txt
npm --prefix agentic-workflows-v2/ui install

The root tools package is installed first, and the langchain extra provides the default named-workflow adapter. The same steps, with a PowerShell variant, are in Installation.

Verify the CLI:

agentic version
agentic list workflows

docs.title: 2. Create the input file
docs.text:
agentic run --input accepts a JSON file path, not inline JSON. The deterministic workflow requires one string named input_text. The repository ships a ready-made input at agentic-workflows-v2/tests/fixtures/deterministic_input.json that you can pass directly. To create your own:

Bash:

printf '{"input_text":"hello"}\n' > /tmp/agentic-input.json

PowerShell:

'{"input_text":"hello"}' |
  Set-Content -Encoding ascii .\agentic-input.json

Use -Encoding ascii (or the shipped fixture) here. Windows PowerShell 5.1 writes a byte-order mark with -Encoding utf8, and the CLI rejects a BOM-prefixed file with Unexpected UTF-8 BOM. PowerShell 7 does not add one.

docs.title: 3. Run the workflow
docs.text:
Bash:

AGENTIC_NO_LLM=1 agentic run test_deterministic \
  --input /tmp/agentic-input.json

PowerShell:

$env:AGENTIC_NO_LLM = "1"
agentic run test_deterministic --input .\agentic-input.json

The expected status is:

Status: SUCCESS

The run also prints the workflow outputs, processed_text and step_count.

test_deterministic has two tier-0 agent steps:

  1. step1 reads and processes input_text.
  2. step2 waits for step1 and counts the processed characters.

Tier-0 agents run deterministic Python handlers on both execution engines, so test_deterministic never calls a model. AGENTIC_NO_LLM=1 is a safeguard here: it replaces every model call with fixed placeholder text (PlaceholderChatModel on the LangGraph path, a mock backend on the native path), which protects you from an accidental provider call if you move on to an LLM-backed workflow. It does not test response quality. The command may log input-mapping or tool-provider warnings while still completing successfully.

Add --verbose to print the execution plan and step result table:

agentic run test_deterministic \
  --input /tmp/agentic-input.json \
  --verbose

docs.title: 4. Save the result
docs.text:
Use --output to write a JSON summary of the run. A relative path works the same in every shell:

agentic run test_deterministic \
  --input /tmp/agentic-input.json \
  --output result.json

PowerShell:

agentic run test_deterministic `
  --input .\agentic-input.json `
  --output .\result.json

Whichever engine ran, the file holds the CLI summary, not the full WorkflowResult model:

  • workflow_name;
  • status, lowercase (for example success);
  • outputs, the workflow's declared outputs (processed_text and step_count for test_deterministic);
  • steps, a map of step name to status, outputs, and error;
  • errors; and
  • elapsed_seconds.

Model fields such as run_id, overall_status, step_results, and final_output are not written. Inspect the result:

python -c "import json; d=json.load(open('result.json')); print(d['status'], d['outputs'])"

PowerShell:

(Get-Content .\result.json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json) | Select-Object status, outputs

docs.title: 5. Check both adapters
docs.text:
The named workflow path defaults to LangGraph. Run the same definition through the native engine:

agentic run test_deterministic \
  --input /tmp/agentic-input.json \
  --adapter native

Or compare both:

agentic compare test_deterministic \
  --input /tmp/agentic-input.json \
  --adapters native,langchain

Both runs should succeed. A failed side makes agentic compare exit non-zero.

docs.title: 6. Confirm the approval gate fails closed
docs.text:
High-impact tools (shell, file_write, build_app, http_post, and others) need approval from a registered ApprovalProvider. A fresh install registers none, so the call is denied before the tool body runs. From the repository root, with the environment active:

python -m pytest agentic-workflows-v2/tests/test_approval_gates.py -k fails_closed -q

See Known limitations section 4.3 for what the gate covers today.

docs.title: 7. Validate another workflow
docs.text:
Validation checks schema, dependencies, cycles, and LangGraph compilation without calling a provider:

agentic validate code_review --verbose
agentic run code_review --dry-run

Do not use placeholder mode as proof that an LLM-backed workflow produces valid business output. The placeholder is fixed text. Workflows that require JSON, source code, tool calls, or typed artifacts can fail or produce unresolved outputs by design.

For a real model-backed run:

  1. copy .env.example to .env;
  2. set one supported provider credential;
  3. unset AGENTIC_NO_LLM; and
  4. supply the inputs required by the selected workflow.

See Configuration and No-LLM mode.

docs.title: 8. Open the dashboard
docs.text:
On Windows, just dev starts the backend and the UI, and just dev-stop stops both. Without just, use two terminals with the environment active.

Terminal 1:

AGENTIC_NO_LLM=1 agentic serve --port 8010 --no-open

PowerShell:

$env:AGENTIC_NO_LLM = "1"
agentic serve --port 8010 --no-open

Terminal 2:

npm --prefix agentic-workflows-v2/ui run dev

The UI is at http://127.0.0.1:5173 and the API at http://127.0.0.1:8010 (OpenAPI at /docs). Vite proxies /api and /ws to port 8010 by default. agentic serve itself defaults to port 8000, so pass --port 8010 to match the proxy. The five-minute demo walks through the dashboard.

docs.title: 0. Executive summary
docs.text: Snapshot: origin/main @ c3b2d328 (2026-10-12, after tafreeman/agentic-runtime-platform#387), inventoried from a clean detached worktree so in-flight branch work does not skew the counts. In-flight work is reported separately in §9. Git and PR state in this repo moves hourly; re-run the scripts before acting on any count.

docs.title: What this repository is
docs.text:
A tier-routed, multi-agent LLM workflow runtime. YAML workflows compile to a DAG. The DAG runs either on a native Kahn's-algorithm asyncio executor or on a LangGraph adapter (the default for named workflows). Each step names a capability tier, never a model. SmartModelRouter resolves the tier to a provider through three-state circuit breakers and bulkheads. A FastAPI server streams execution over WebSocket and SSE to a React 19 "ARP Console". A fail-closed governance layer (human-in-the-loop tool approval and an SSRF egress guard) sits in front of tool dispatch. Around the runtime are:

  • an offline evaluation harness (agentic-v2-eval, being migrated to the external agentic-evalkit);
  • a shared tools/ package (model probes, benchmarks);
  • Lean 4 proofs of the scheduler.

docs.title: Shape at a glance
docs.text: Area Size (main @ c3b2d328) Health Runtime agentic_v2 ~244 modules, ~62k LOC, 22 subpackages Active; 8 modules over 800 LOC; 17% of LOC excluded from the coverage gate Python tests 287 files, ~4,600 test functions 80% gate on agentic_v2; tools/tests runs with 11 deselected tests UI (agentic-workflows-v2/ui) 203 TS/TSX files, 10 routes, 66 unit test files, 13 Playwright specs Active; Evidence Ledger redesign in flight (#388) HTTP API 53 /api routes and a WebSocket 7 routes have no UI caller Workflows 9 YAML definitions 2 are test fixtures (one duplicates the other) CI 18 workflow files, 20 jobs in ci.yml One referenced workflow and one bicepparam file are missing Docs 133 markdown docs, 55 ADRs (5 Proposed) Many root status docs are stale (HANDOFF, ROADMAP, KNOWN_LIMITATIONS)

docs.title: Top findings (cross-section)
docs.text:
1. Generated chat contract is checked by CI but never used. ui/src/api/chat_request.generated.ts and chat_stream_event.generated.ts pass the wire-format-drift gate, but nothing imports them. The UI uses hand-written copies in ui/src/api/types.ts. A backend schema change would therefore stay green while the UI types silently drift (§3.5, §4.6).
  2. A silent broken import disables the benchmark LLM-judge. tools/agents/benchmarks/evaluation_pipeline.py:34-40 imports reporting helpers from llm_evaluator, but they moved to evaluator_reporting.py. A try/except ImportError swallows the failure, so HAS_LLM_EVALUATOR is always False. This is the real cause of the 10 deselected TestEvaluateTaskOutputLlm tests (§5.6).
  3. There is no route to submit HITL approval decisions. ApprovalRequiredEvent and ApprovalDecisionEvent exist, but no HTTP or WebSocket handler accepts a decision. The WebSocket also ignores every client message, including the node_config_update frames the UI sends (§3.1, §4.6).
  4. The two engines aren't interchangeable. model_override, persona, observers and model_params are honoured only by the LangChain adapter. There are two parallel YAML parsers (workflows/loader.py and langchain/config.py) and two WorkflowRunners. docs/WORKFLOW_AUTHORING.md mentions none of this (§2, §5.1).
  5. Dead code is small and well-bounded. Deletion candidates:
  6. Python: engine/patterns.py (empty stub), models/llm.py (legacy adapter scheduled for deletion by ADR-042), tools/core/{cache,response_cache,prompt_db}.py (cache.py doesn't even import), tools/llm/list_gemini.py.
  7. UI: nine unused shadcn primitives (making react-resizable-panels a dead dependency), BBox, BSpark, useNodeConfigUpdate, the NodeConfigOverlay prototype, PrototypeLabPage, and the test-only SettingsPage (§2, §4.6, §5.6).
  8. Config and docs have drifted from the code:
  9. .env.example documents 5 keys nothing reads and omits about 6 keys the code reads (§3.8).
  10. The workspace CLAUDE.md §7 and ADR-042 quote the EK and EVK pins as 0.3.x, but main pins executionkit>=0.4.0,<0.5.0 and agentic-evalkit>=0.4.1,<0.5.0 (§1.3).
  11. portfolio-context.md says 17 CI jobs; there are 20 (§6.1).
  12. docs/deployment-guide.md still lists the deleted manifest-temperature-check.yml (§6.9).
  13. Toolchain versions disagree. .nvmrc says Node 20, CI uses 22, Dockerfile.ui uses 26.11. Pre-commit ruff is 0.16.5, but the dev group requires ≥0.16.10. nginx.conf proxies neither /api nor /ws (§4.1, §6.3).
  14. Docs still advertise retired things.
  15. docs/configuration.md:63 and docs/getting-started/installation.md:168 still list GitHub Models, which was retired on 2026-07-30 (ADR-016).
  16. docs/deployment-guide.md:13 says CI has "fourteen jobs"; it has 20.
  17. ADR-008 says Proposed in its file but Accepted in ADR-INDEX.md.
  18. check_docs_refs.py scans only 19 of about 205 markdown files, so most of docs/** is never link-checked (§8).
  19. About 1.2 GB of local-only clutter is on disk.
  20. Safe to delete: caches and build outputs, for example .mypy_cache/ (620 MB), .cache/ (134 MB), proofs/.lake/ (116 MB) and site/.
  21. Also deletable: the __pycache__-only orphan packages agentic_v2/rag/ and agentic_v2/memoryctl/, and agentic-workflows-v2/New folder (2)/.
  22. Keep: runs/, the replay DBs and .env, which hold user data (§7).
  23. Some work exists only on this machine. At extract time:
  24. Unpushed or uncommitted: about 2.1k lines of untracked Evidence Ledger components, probe-tooling edits, and a tech-debt plan on the unpushed docs/tech_debt_plans branch.
  25. feature/criterion_aggregation: no PR open.
  26. Stalled: #384 (38 dependency bumps, 26 failing checks) (§9).

docs.title: How this inventory was produced
docs.text:
All counts come from scripts committed alongside this document. Re-run them against a fresh origin/main worktree:

git worktree add --detach ../arp-main-inventory origin/main
ARP_INVENTORY_REPO=../arp-main-inventory .venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/inventory/run_all.py
.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/inventory/assemble.py
uv run --no-project --with markdown python scripts/inventory/render_html.py
Script Extracts scripts/inventory/fs_inventory.py Per-directory tracked and untracked counts, sizes, last-commit age, large files, orphan __pycache__-only packages scripts/inventory/py_inventory.py AST per module: LOC, classes (Pydantic, Protocol, Enum, …), functions, FastAPI routes, import graph (absolute, relative and lazy), env-var reads, TODO markers, test references, orphan candidates scripts/inventory/ui_inventory.py TS/TSX import graph, exports, /api calls, routes, unused and test-only files, external package usage scripts/inventory/meta_inventory.py Workflow YAML steps, CI jobs, ADR statuses, doc staleness and broken links, dependency manifests, git branches, worktrees and PRs scripts/inventory/assemble.py / render_html.py Concatenate the section files and render the Superdesign-styled HTML report

The section narratives (§1–§9) were written by parallel research agents working from that data and the code, each told to verify its claims. Read them with these limitations in mind:

  • Orphan detection is a candidate list, not a verdict. Registry and string-based wiring evades static import graphs. Every "unused" item in §2, §4 and §5 was re-checked with grep.
  • The env-var extractor misses some reads. It doesn't catch reads through pydantic Settings fields or get_secret(); §3.8 corrects for this by hand.
  • File age isn't a reliable staleness signal for the UI. A broad restyle sweep touched most files within the last week.
  • Items marked "(unverified)" were not confirmed.

docs.title: Layers
docs.text: Layer Responsibility Primary code 1. Workflow definition YAML (inputs, steps, depends_on, when, loop_until/loop_max, agent, tools, outputs) agentic_v2/workflows/definitions/*.yaml, workflows/loader.py 2. Compile / validate YAML -> typed definitions -> DAG; rejects missing deps (MissingDependencyError) and cycles (CycleDetectedError) agentic_v2/engine/dag.py:19,28,38, engine/step.py 3. Engine seam AdapterRegistry (thread-safe singleton) maps "native" / "langchain" to engine classes agentic_v2/adapters/registry.py, adapters/native/engine.py, adapters/langchain/engine.py 4a. Native executor Kahn in-degree wavefront scheduling on asyncio, cascade skip, top-level timeout, OTel spans agentic_v2/engine/dag_executor.py (718 lines) 4b. LangGraph adapter Builds a StateGraph from the same YAML; join-once edge wiring (ADR-062) agentic_v2/langchain/ (graph.py, graph_wiring.py, runner.py, state.py) 5. Agents and steps tier{N}_{role} agent names resolved to functions/agents (tier0_* deterministic handlers; others LLM-backed); Markdown persona prompts engine/agent_resolver.py:306-310,644-660, agentic_v2/agents/, agentic_v2/prompts/*.md 6. Tools and MCP Tool registry + builtins (file, git, shell, http, code exec, build, memory, search, ...), MCP client stack agentic_v2/tools/, tools/builtin/, integrations/mcp/ 7. Governance and security Approval gate (fail-closed), SSRF URL guard, sanitization detectors, AST expression sandbox governance/approval.py, security/url_guard.py, middleware/detectors/, engine/expressions.py 8. Model routing ModelTier 0-5, per-tier fallback chains from curated registry, circuit breakers, bulkheads, rate-limit tracker, Redis CAS state models/router.py:33, models/smart_router.py (1078 lines), models/model_registry.py, models/redis_state.py 9. Providers/backends Ollama, OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Claude subscription/SDK, OpenRouter, local discovery (Ollama, LM Studio, Lemonade, Foundry Local, Docker Model Runner) models/backends*.py, models/*_discovery.py, models/client.py 10. Server FastAPI app, route groups under /api, WebSocket, SSE, auth (API key, JWT/OIDC), rate limit, tenant, audit log, replay store, SPA serving agentic_v2/server/ 11. Observability OpenTelemetry tracer, Prometheus metrics, tracing middleware integrations/otel.py, integrations/metrics.py, server/middleware/{tracing,metrics}.py 12. Scoring/eval Runtime scoring of saved runs (rubrics, LLM judge, multidimensional); bridge to agentic-evalkit agentic_v2/scoring/, scoring/evalkit_bridge.py 13. UI React 19 console; generated TS wire types agentic-workflows-v2/ui/src/ 14. Shared package Root agentic-tools (tools/): LLM clients, probes, model inventory, caches, prompt DB, benchmarks tools/

docs.title: 1.5 Theories, concepts and patterns implemented
docs.text:
# Concept What it is Where implemented ADR 1 Kahn's topological DAG execution Track per-step in-degree at runtime; launch every zero-in-degree step concurrently (wavefront); unlock dependents on completion engine/dag.py (DAG, topological order, validate), engine/dag_executor.py (_schedule_ready_steps, _unlock_downstream, _scheduling_loop) ADR-001/002/003, ADR-019 2 Cascade skip / honest status Failed step's transitive dependents are SKIPPED with a reason; run is SUCCESS only if nothing failed or was dropped engine/dag_executor.py (_cascade_skip, _mark_skipped), agents/orchestrator.py ADR-060 3 Formal verification of the scheduler Lean 4 model of DAGExecutor proves safety, no duplicates / bounded parallelism, completeness, honest status over every legal completion order; a replay test ties model to code on sampled schedules (not a proof of the Python) proofs/Scheduler.lean, proofs/Scheduler/, proofs/Main.lean, tests/engine/test_dag_executor_lean_replay.py (named in proofs/README.md, not opened) ADR-060 4 Engine swap behind a Protocol seam Structural typing.Protocol contracts + thread-safe registry core/protocols.py, adapters/registry.py ADR-001, ADR-020; ADR-031 (single-engine, not adopted) 5 Join-once semantics for superstep engines Each step runs once after all deps even on LangGraph langchain/graph_wiring.py (wire_graph_edges, wire_dependency_edges, build_loop_exit_map, add_loop_edge) ADR-062 6 Capability-tier routing Steps request tier 0 (deterministic) to 5 (premium cloud); router resolves via per-tier fallback chains from a curated registry models/router.py (ModelTier, register_chain, DEFAULT_CHAINS), models/smart_router.py, models/model_registry.py ADR-040, ADR-059, ADR-051 7 Three-state circuit breaker CLOSED / OPEN / HALF_OPEN per provider with single-probe lock; CircuitResolvedError when a prior probe already resolved the circuit models/smart_router.py (execute_with_bulkhead, ~lines 814-1016), models/model_stats.py ADR-001/002/003 (ADR-002A) 8 Bulkheads Per-provider semaphores prevent cascade failure models/smart_router.py:190,256 ADR-002A 9 Shared breaker state via compare-and-swap Lua-script atomic CAS in Redis keeps counters exact under concurrent writers; evidence is a k6 run plus an exact-sum worker test models/redis_state.py, docs/flagship.md, load/ no dedicated ADR found (unverified) 10 Health, cooldown, rate-limit awareness Honour retry guidance, cooldowns, HTTP-status error classification models/smart_router.py (CooldownConfig), models/rate_limit_tracker.py, models/retry_utils.py none 11 Majority-vote consensus / self-consistency Same prompt N times, deterministic tier-0 vote, min_agreement threshold engine/consensus.py (majority_vote, self_consistency), engine/agent_resolver.py:309 (tier0_consensus), workflows/definitions/consensus_review.yaml ADR-023 (EK relationship) 12 Plan tribunal (multi-judge panel) Five persona judges, two-stage deterministic vote, dissent recorded, split ruling never presented as a decision workflows/definitions/plan_tribunal.yaml none found 13 Bounded iterative review loop loop_until + loop_max review-rework cycles; verification gate/loop for post-step checks workflows/definitions/iterative_review.yaml, engine/step.py, engine/verification.py (VerificationGate, VerificationLoop) ADR-019 for timeout; loop-specific ADR unverified 14 Adaptive decomposition / orchestrator Orchestrator plans subtasks, validates plan as a DAG, runs with max_parallel, fallback chains, escalation agents/orchestrator.py, orchestrator_planning.py, orchestrator_models.py, governance/escalation.py ADR-029, ADR-025, ADR-060 15 LLM-as-judge rubric scoring Rubric criteria scored by a judge model; multidimensional profiles scoring/judge.py (LLMJudge, JudgeResponseProvider), scoring/rubrics/, scoring/multidimensional_scoring.py, prompts/judges/, agentic-v2-eval/src/ ADR-009, ADR-010, ADR-032, ADR-044 16 Discriminated-union wire format + codegen Pydantic Field(discriminator="type") unions -> JSON Schema -> generated TS; docs.title: Known limitations that bound the architecture (docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md)
docs.text: Ref Limitation 1.1 Wire format generated for 8 shapes only; others manually mirrored 1.2 80% coverage gate scopes out optional provider/plugin modules ([tool.coverage.run] omit) 2.1 LangChain adapter needs a separate extras install 3.1 Blocking CI does not prove live provider behaviour 4.1, 4.2 Rate limiting and auth throttle are in-process only (multi-replica caveat) 4.3 Human approval gates are programmatic only; no UI pause/resume yet 4.4 SSRF guard cannot fully close DNS rebinding without network-layer egress control 4.5 X-Tenant-ID is client-supplied and spoofable by default 4.12-4.14 Model inventory command fails from repo root; onnx: IDs unusable for exact-model chat; strict weight verification not wired into every loader 4.15 Eleven tools/tests cases assert a removed API; ci.yml now lists a tools-tests job, so whether this is still current is unverified

docs.title: 2. Runtime backend — components & data structures (agentic_v2)
docs.text: Scope: agentic-workflows-v2/agentic_v2/ at origin/main c3b2d328 (clean worktree ../arp-main-inventory). 244 Python modules, 61,892 LOC (inventory counts, __init__ files included). Only console script: [project.scripts] agentic = "agentic_v2.cli:main" (agentic-workflows-v2/pyproject.toml:130-131). Section 3 covers the HTTP/WS API; section 5 covers the YAML workflow definitions; this section covers the Python components behind them.

docs.title: 2.0 How to read the tables
docs.text:
• LOC — physical lines from docs/inventory/data/py_inventory.json.
  • used by — distinct in-package modules importing the module, recomputed by AST with relative imports resolved. The raw imported_by field misses from .x import y, which is why contracts.schemas and governance.escalation looked orphaned there. A (pkg) row counts importers of the package itself.
  • tests — number of test files (agentic-workflows-v2/tests/**, repo-root tests/**) that contain the module path or one of its public class/function names. A name-match heuristic: 0 is reliable (no reference anywhere); a positive count is an upper bound on real coverage.
  • status — Active = imported by another runtime module; Test-only = imported by no runtime module but referenced by tests; Orphan? = neither (only models.llm after verification; see 2.24). Flags >800 LOC, TODO, no tests are appended. Active (pkg) marks __init__ re-export hubs.
  • Purpose is the module docstring first line; where empty, the first public class/function docstring; a few docstring-less modules got a hand-written purpose.

The table below lists the ones that matter; WIRE marks the eight wire-format contract models.

docs.title: 2.23.1 The 8 wire-format contract models (Python to JSON Schema to TypeScript)
docs.text:
Pipeline: Pydantic model, then agentic-workflows-v2/scripts/generate_ts_types.py writes the aggregate JSON Schema into agentic-workflows-v2/tests/schemas/, then npm run generate:types (from ui/) emits the *.generated.ts mirror. CI job wire-format-drift fails on any mismatch (.claude/rules/ci.md, ADR-014). The generated headers say "AUTO-GENERATED — DO NOT EDIT BY HAND".

# Pydantic model defined in JSON Schema (agentic-workflows-v2/tests/schemas/) TS mirror (agentic-workflows-v2/ui/src/api/) TS LOC 1 ExecutionEvent (discriminated union) agentic_v2/contracts/events.py events.schema.json events.generated.ts 182 2 StepResultRecord agentic_v2/contracts/messages.py step_result.schema.json step_result.generated.ts 70 3 DAGResponse agentic_v2/server/models.py dag_response.schema.json dag_response.generated.ts 93 4 WorkflowInputSchemaResponse agentic_v2/server/models.py workflow_input_schema.schema.json workflow_input_schema.generated.ts 96 5 WorkflowEditorStep agentic_v2/server/models.py workflow_editor_step.schema.json workflow_editor_step.generated.ts 66 6 RunsSummaryResponse agentic_v2/server/models.py runs_summary.schema.json runs_summary.generated.ts 30 7 ChatRequest (RootModel union) agentic_v2/contracts/chat.py chat_request.schema.json chat_request.generated.ts 186 8 ChatStreamEvent (discriminated union) agentic_v2/contracts/chat.py chat_stream_event.schema.json chat_stream_event.generated.ts 57

Source of the mapping: module docstring and constants at agentic-workflows-v2/scripts/generate_ts_types.py:9-53. agentic-workflows-v2/ui/src/api/ also holds hand-written client.ts, types.ts, websocket.ts, hardware.ts (not generated).

Separate from the eight: agentic-workflows-v2/tests/schemas/ holds 24 further per-model snapshots (AgentMessage.json, ChatDoneEvent.json, CodeReviewOutput.json, ReviewReport.json, StepResult.json, TaskInput.json, WorkflowResult.json, ...; 32 files total including the 8 aggregates), written by agentic-workflows-v2/scripts/generate_schemas.py and checked by agentic-workflows-v2/tests/test_schema_drift.py. These have no TS mirror (inferred from absence of matching *.generated.ts).

docs.text:
py_inventory.json flagged five non-test modules as orphan_candidate. Its import graph ignores relative imports and lazy (in-function) imports, so each was re-verified by grep over agentic-workflows-v2/, scripts/, tools/, .github/, pyproject files and YAML (searched for dotted paths, from .x import, importlib/string references, entry points, __init__ re-exports). Verdicts:

module LOC verdict evidence agentic_v2.contracts.schemas 385 Used (false positive) Imported relatively by agentic_v2/contracts/__init__.py:73 (from .schemas import (...)), then re-exported to agentic_v2/__init__.py, core/__init__.py and consumed by agents/architect.py, agents/base.py, agents/orchestrator*.py, agents/reviewer.py, agents/test_agent.py, agents/implementations/claude_agent.py through agentic_v2.contracts. Exercised by agentic-workflows-v2/tests/test_contracts.py (code-generation/code-review schema classes) and the tests/schemas/TaskInput.json family. agentic_v2.governance.escalation 137 Used (false positive, lazy import) Re-exported by agentic_v2/governance/__init__.py; consumed by a function-local import in agentic_v2/agents/orchestrator.py:393 (from ..governance import HandoffSummary, route_handoff) in _emit_escalation_handoff; tested by agentic-workflows-v2/tests/test_escalation_handoff.py (7 tests) and referenced from tests/test_orchestrator_behavior.py. agentic_v2.agents.implementations.agent_loader 118 Used dynamically (public API only; untested) Imported in agents/implementations/__init__.py:31-32 inside a try/except ImportError guard (optional [claude] extra) and re-exported as AGENTS/load_agents. Runs load_agents() at import (agent_loader.py:155), reading .md agent files from a shipped dir plus AGENTIC_EXTERNAL_AGENTS_DIR. No in-repo consumer of AGENTS/load_agents was found outside that __init__, no test exercises it (only tests/test_env_template_contract.py mentions the env var), and pyproject.toml coverage-omits agents/implementations/*. Effectively an external-facing convenience with no internal caller. agentic_v2.engine.patterns (package) 3 Truly unused (empty stub) engine/patterns/__init__.py is a docstring plus __all__ = []; no importer, no test, no YAML/string reference. docs.title: 3. Interfaces — HTTP/WebSocket API, CLI, contracts, configuration
docs.text: Source of truth: clean origin/main worktree at revision c3b2d328 (../arp-main-inventory). All paths are repo-relative. S/ = agentic-workflows-v2/agentic_v2/server/, R/ = agentic-workflows-v2/agentic_v2/server/routes/.

docs.title: 3.1 HTTP API surface
docs.text:
The app factory is create_app() in S/app.py. Every router in R/ is mounted with prefix="/api" (S/app.py:158-167) except the WebSocket router (/ws/..., no prefix, S/app.py:168), the optional Prometheus mount at /metrics, and the SPA catch-all. That gives 55 decorated route handlers (py_inventory.json): 53 under /api, 1 WebSocket, 1 SPA fallback.

Auth column legend: key = requires AGENTIC_API_KEY bearer/X-API-Key when that env var is set (otherwise the server is open and S/lifespan.py:263-266 logs a warning); public = exempt in is_public_path (S/auth.py:54-57, 257-269); tenant = also resolves Depends(get_tenant_context) (agentic_v2/core/tenant.py:64, header-based tenant id).
